:::{#thm-eigen-shift-power}
#### Eigenvalues of shifts and powers

Let $\vecf{v}$ be an eigenvector of a $p \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$ for the eigenvalue $\eigval$
(@def-eigenvalue). Then

1. $\vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{A} + s\,\matr{I}_p$ for $\eigval + s$, for every number $s$;
2. $\vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{A}^k$ (@def-matrix-power) for $\eigval^k$,
   for every positive integer $k$.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**

$$
\ba
(\matr{A} + s\,\matr{I}_p)\,\vecf{v}
&= \matr{A} \vecf{v} + (s\,\matr{I}_p)\,\vecf{v}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib)}
\\
&= \matr{A} \vecf{v} + s\,(\matr{I}_p \vecf{v})
&& \text{(@thm-scalar-matmul)}
\\
&= \eigval \vecf{v} + s\,(\matr{I}_p \vecf{v})
&& \text{(eigenvector)}
\\
&= \eigval \vecf{v} + s \vecf{v}
&& \text{(@thm-identity)}
\\
&= (\eigval + s)\,\vecf{v}.
&& \text{(add entrywise)}
\ea
$$

**Part 2, by [induction](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mcs/proof-writing.html#def-proof-by-induction) on $k$.**
For $k = 1$ it is the assumption.
If $\matr{A}^{k-1} \vecf{v} = \eigval^{k-1} \vecf{v}$, then

$$
\ba
\matr{A}^k \vecf{v}
&= \matr{A}\,(\matr{A}^{k-1} \vecf{v})
&& \text{(@def-matrix-power, @thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{A}\,(\eigval^{k-1} \vecf{v})
&& \text{(induction hypothesis)}
\\
&= \eigval^{k-1}\,(\matr{A} \vecf{v})
&& \text{(@thm-scalar-matmul)}
\\
&= \eigval^{k-1}\,(\eigval \vecf{v})
&& \text{(eigenvector)}
\\
&= \eigval^k \vecf{v}.
&& \text{(multiply the numbers)}
\ea
$$

In both parts $\vecf{v} \ne \vzero$, so $\vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector.

:::
